circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island, has served as the Formula One calendar's traditional season finale since 2009. The venue represents the second Middle Eastern addition to the F1 circuit roster, following Bahrain and preceding Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside supporting motorsport events. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 licence for international racing competition.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit was originally established as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following a redesign and shortening of the track, it was relaunched under a new name and resumed hosting the Grand Prix in the late 1990s and early 2000s.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital positioned along Baku Boulevard, measuring 6. 003 km per lap to rank as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The circuit first hosted the European Grand Prix in 2016 before becoming home to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and hosted the first Formula One race ever staged in the Middle East that same year. The Grade 1 FIA-licensed venue has since become a regular stop on the Formula One calendar while also accommodating various other racing categories including endurance competitions and multiple circuit configurations.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located near Barcelona in Montmeló, this 4. 657-kilometre Spanish circuit combines extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for all racing disciplines. The venue features FIA Grade 1 certification and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: The 7-kilometre Belgian circuit in Wallonia has hosted Formula One racing since 1950 and served as the venue for the inaugural world championship season. It has maintained continuous Grand Prix status annually since 1985, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km street circuit that serves as the permanent home of the Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the track has hosted various international motorsport series including sportscar championships and open-wheel racing events.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading district, this Chinese motorsport facility is primarily recognized as the host of the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The venue also accommodates electric racing events starting in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone is an English racing venue positioned near villages in Northamptonshire that inaugurated the British Grand Prix in 1948 and hosted the inaugural World Championship race two years later. Following decades of rotation among three circuits, the Grand Prix became a permanent fixture at Silverstone from 1987 onwards, while the facility also serves as home to British MotoGP competition.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: Located near Budapest in Mogyoród, the 4. 381 km Hungaroring hosted Formula One's first grand prix in the Eastern Bloc when it debuted in 1986, constructed in just eight months following a recommendation to Bernie Ecclestone from a Hungarian associate. The newly built permanent circuit replaced initial plans for a street layout within Budapest's Népliget park, with the inaugural race dedicated to János Drapál, Hungary's pioneering motorcycle Grand Prix winner.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Situated near Milan in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale di Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit established in 1922, making it Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venue and the fourth globally. The track has hosted the Italian Grand Prix annually since 1949, except for a 1980 closure for renovations, establishing itself as one of only three circuits present throughout Formula One's entire history, and earns its nickname "Temple of Speed" from its characteristically long straightaways and quick-corner design.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807-kilometer Japanese motorsport venue situated in Mie Prefecture and managed by Honda Mobilityland. The track, which accommodates 155,000 spectators, has become iconic as the primary host of Formula One racing in Japan and serves as a centerpiece for the Super Formula championship.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, running alongside the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its concentration of major hotels and casinos. The layout incorporates several iconic venues including MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas as it winds through the urban landscape.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit honoring two Mexican racing brothers who both perished in fatal accidents during the 1960s and early 1970s. The venue has served as host to Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix across three distinct eras, most recently resuming the event in 2015 on its current configuration after a 23-year absence, now officially designated as the Mexico City Grand Prix since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens that stretches 3. 363 miles with 19 corners, achieving average qualifying speeds near 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One, it joined the championship calendar in 2022 and has since become the primary venue for the Miami Grand Prix.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street track that winds through Monte Carlo and La Condamine neighborhoods, following the harbor's perimeter in the Principality of Monaco. Though officially named after the circuit itself, it is widely known as Monte Carlo due to its location predominantly within that district.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted the Dutch Grand Prix from 2021 to 2026. The venue earned its "Roller coaster in the Dunes" nickname from its distinctive design featuring dramatically banked corners and significant elevation changes that wind through the North Sea dunes, creating a uniquely challenging racing experience.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Located north of Doha in Qatar, the Lusail International Circuit is a 5. 419 km track featuring a lengthy 1. 068 km main straight and holding an FIA Grade 1 license.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, Brazil, Interlagos is a 4. 309 km counterclockwise racing facility that opened in 1940 and was later renamed in 1985 to commemorate the late Formula One driver José Carlos Pace. The track has hosted numerous major motorsport events and features additional amenities including a karting circuit dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront that has hosted the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its inaugural running in 2021. The circuit also began accommodating Formula E racing in 2025, establishing itself as a dual-category motorsport destination.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through downtown Singapore around the Marina Bay waterfront, incorporating the Downtown Core and Kallang districts into its racing layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya stretches 4. 657 kilometres and features a balanced mix of lengthy straights and varied turn configurations that test all aspects of racing performance. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 FIA facility hosting multiple international motorsport series, most notably the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track accommodates MotoGP, NASCAR, and World Endurance Championship events, while previously welcoming IndyCar, rallycross, and sports car racing competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a dual Thai-British racing driver currently competing for Williams in Formula One, representing Thailand on the international stage.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has claimed two world championship titles with Renault in 2005 and 2006, along with 32 Grand Prix victories across 23 seasons. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including winning the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship and two Le Mans 24 Hours victories, making him the sole driver to have captured both the Formula One drivers' title and the World Endurance championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Andrea Kimi Antonelli, an Italian motorsport competitor, drives for Mercedes in Formula One and has claimed nine race victories since entering the sport in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British motorsport competitor currently racing for Haas in Formula One.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabi Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One representing Audi, bringing his racing talent to the sport's top tier.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One after a lengthy career spanning 13 seasons. He achieved two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during his Mercedes years in 2019 and 2020, and has secured 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his tenure in the sport.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Colapinto is an Argentine driver currently racing in Formula One for the Alpine team. He has established himself as a competitor on the sport's top racing tier.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: French driver Pierre Gasly competes for Alpine in Formula One and previously secured a Grand Prix victory at the 2020 Italian round while racing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: French-Algerian driver Isack Alexandre Hadjar represents France in Formula One, currently racing for Red Bull Racing.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari who has secured seven world championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record. He holds numerous racing records including the most career victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races in Formula One for Audi and has achieved notable success in endurance competition, including a victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans while driving for Porsche in 2015.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver for Ferrari, finished as championship runner-up in 2022 and has accumulated nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine seasons in Formula One.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver currently competing in the FIA World Endurance Championship with BMW through WRT, while also undertaking part-time NASCAR commitments with Trackhouse Racing. He previously had two separate stints in Formula One, racing between 2014-2020 and again from 2022-2024.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver competing for McLaren, claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship. Across his eight seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The Monaco-born competitor achieved a Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from 15 seasons in the sport. He finished second in the 2023 drivers' championship while with Red Bull and has accumulated six Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver competing for McLaren in Formula One, has secured nine Grand Prix victories since joining the series four seasons ago.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by the moniker "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One over fourteen years from 2011 through 2024, securing eight race victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured eight Grand Prix victories throughout his eight seasons in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four race victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who competed in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to endurance racing. He currently races in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously driven LMP2 machinery in the IMSA SportsCar Championship.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian driver currently racing for Aston Martin in Formula One.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, held a full-time Formula One seat from 2021 through 2025 before transitioning to a reserve role for Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: A Dutch-Belgian driver competing for Red Bull Racing, Verstappen has secured four consecutive world championship titles spanning from 2021 to 2024. Over his 12-season career, he has accumulated 73 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is a Chinese racing driver currently functioning as a reserve driver for Cadillac in Formula One. He previously competed in the sport from 2022 to 2024 and holds the distinction of being the sole Chinese driver to have raced in Formula One.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based squad operated as Renault's works team before being rebranded as Alpine for the 2021 season to showcase the French manufacturer's sports car division. Renault maintained control of the operation until withdrawing from Formula One following the 2025 campaign.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has maintained a presence in Formula One through different organizational structures, with its current racing operation competing under the Aston Martin Aramco banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari represents the motorsport arm of the Italian luxury carmaker Ferrari and stands as Formula One's oldest continuously competing outfit, having participated in every world championship season since 1950. The team, colloquially known as "the Prancing Horse" after its iconic emblem, holds the distinction of being the sport's most accomplished outfit by historical measure.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: The American-licensed Formula One team, established by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas in 2014, commenced racing operations in 2016. Leadership changed in early 2024 when Ayao Komatsu took over as team principal from Guenther Steiner, who had held the position since the team's founding.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Founded by Peter Sauber in 1970, this Swiss engineering firm established itself in motorsport through endurance racing success, including the 1989 Le Mans 24 Hours victory. The operation entered Formula One in 1993 and competed for three decades before being acquired by Audi in 2024, making it the fourth-longest-serving constructor by race entries when it departed the championship.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that competes under McLaren Mastercard F1 Team. The squad operates as part of the McLaren Group, with full ownership residing under Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 in both manufacturing and team ownership roles. The current operation, Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team, is headquartered in Brackley and races under a German licence, with ownership shared equally among Mercedes-Benz Group, Toto Wolff, and Ineos as of January 2022. The marque is traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows" in motorsport circles.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that commenced competition in 2024, operating as one of two Red Bull-owned squads alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility near its sister team in Milton Keynes, the outfit functions as part of the Austrian conglomerate's motorsport portfolio.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor based in Faenza that entered the championship in 2024 as Red Bull GmbH's second racing operation, alongside Red Bull Racing. The team maintains a secondary facility in Milton Keynes to coordinate with its sister outfit.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, operating under an Austrian licence from their English base, emerged as a Formula One competitor in 2005 and has since become one of two series entries controlled by Red Bull GmbH. Christian Horner led the team throughout its twenty-year tenure until his 2025 departure, with Laurent Mekies assuming the leadership role.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, represents the successful continuation of Williams's earlier racing efforts. Currently competing as Atlassian Williams F1 Team, the outfit has maintained its headquarters at a substantial Grove, Oxfordshire facility since its inception.
